summary.oneLiner: Q3FY26 saw a sequential margin contraction to 31% driven by a >25% drop in Argon realizations and one-off costs, masking underlying volume resilience protected by take-or-pay contracts. Management reaffirms a 40% long-term EBITDA margin target as new efficient capacities (Uluberia, East India, North India) commission and power costs optimize via renewable contracts.

one-line thesis: Q3FY26 saw a sequential margin contraction to 31% driven by a >25% drop in Argon realizations and one-off costs, masking underlying volume resilience protected by take-or-pay contracts. Management reaffirms a 40% long-term EBITDA margin target as new efficient capacities (Uluberia, East India, North India) commission and power costs optimize via renewable contracts.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 813 Mn (-9% QoQ, +YoY growth noted but unspecified); EBITDA: INR 253 Mn (31% margin, down from 38% in Q2); PAT: INR 261 Mn (boosted by other income, Total Income INR 974 Mn); Order Book: Not disclosed (long-term take-or-pay contracts); Net Debt: Net Cash of INR 3,550 Mn. One-offs: Elevated other expenses cited as one-off costs impacting Q3 profitability.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Long-term 20-25% CAGR (lumpy execution); Margin: Reaffirmed ~40% long-term EBITDA margin; Order Inflow: Positive traction in solar, few contracts signed; Capex: INR 2,500 Mn (FY26), INR 2,000 Mn (FY27).
order book & pipeline: Revenue model relies on long-term take-or-pay on-site contracts (insulating revenue from volume dips) and merchant sales; specific order book value not quantified; solar segment has signed 'a couple' of contracts.
segment / subsidiary detail: Merchant: Uluberia 2 (220 TPD) commissioned Q3, ramping up. On-site: East India plant (320 TPD) delayed to Q1 FY27. Future: North India bulk plant (220 TPD) targeted H2 FY27; Western India speciality gases plant targeted FY28.
growth verticals / optionality: Entry into solar cell manufacturing gas supply (traded high-purity gases + debulking facility in West India); Semiconductor segment (nascent, no contracts yet); Geographic expansion from East/South to North/West India.
margins & cost dynamics: Q3 margin squeeze due to >25% drop in Argon prices (steel oversupply) and one-off costs. Power is the single largest cost; mitigation via new renewable energy contract signed. New plants expected to be more power-efficient.
capex / expansion: INR 450 Crore allocated across three upcoming projects (East On-site, North Merchant, West Speciality). FY26 guidance INR 2,500 Mn; FY27 guidance INR 2,000 Mn. Equipment lead times are the critical path.
capital allocation: Disciplined capex funded by strong net cash position (INR 3,550 Mn); no debt raise mentioned; focus on organic greenfield expansions.
risks & watch-items: Argon price volatility linked to steel sector cyclicality; Project execution delays (East India plant slipped 2 months); Competition from larger peers (Linde, Inox, Air Products) in solar segment; Import dependency for speciality gases.
management quality / tone: Constructive and resilient; acknowledges Q3 softness as temporary ('worst is over'); emphasizes long-term trajectory over quarterly lumpiness; transparent about delays and pricing headwinds.
non-obvious takeaways: Take-or-pay contracts protected revenue despite customers reducing physical offtake volumes (providing early signal of steel softness without financial impact); Solar gas business is primarily trading/debulking with teens margins, distinct from high-margin ASU manufacturing.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Argon prices down >25% due to steel oversupply | Steel Manufacturers | loser | High | Captive gas plants flooding market, depressing merchant argon realizations for all players including Ellenbarrie. |
| Power cost optimization critical for margin recovery | Renewable Energy Developers | beneficiary | Med | Ellenbarrie signed renewable energy contract to mitigate largest cost component. |
| Need for localized high-purity gas supply for solar manufacturing | Solar Cell Manufacturers | beneficiary | Med | Ellenbarrie setting up western facility to reduce reliance on Chinese imports and handle last-mile delivery. |

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.
themes.driver: Caustic/soda-ash price recovery; utilization ramp on new capacity; energy-cost relief.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Market Leader In 3 states – West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh & Telangana" with a "50+ years rich legacy" (as on 31st March 2026), in an industry the deck describes as "Dominated by Multinational Organizations" where Ellenbarrie is shown as the large domestic player.
- Claims the "Highest transport tankers, cylinders & customer installations in India" and 3rd position (as on 31st March 2026); the extract does not make clear which metric the '3rd' rank attaches to.
- Contract architecture is the stated moat: On-site 15-20 years on take-or-pay with guaranteed return and cost pass-through; Merchant 3-7 years creating network density; Packaged 1-3 years creating network density with bundled offerings and services.
- Customer stickiness: revenue from repeat customers (purchasing for at least 2 consecutive years) was 92% in FY24, 86% in FY25 and 86% in FY26; revenue from customers with more than 10 years' relationship rose ₹1,175 Mn (FY24) → ₹1,221 Mn (FY25) → ₹1,270 Mn (FY26).
- Customer base as on 31st March 2026: 1,498 package customers, 328 bulk customers with 257 bulk customer installations, and 3 onsite customers plus orders for 2 more.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [O&M contract] A work order from NMDC Steel Limited for operation and maintenance of two 1,250 TPD ASU plants at Nagarnar, awarded 6 October 2023 for a five-year term, is EXCLUDED from the company's total capacity calculation because it is an O&M order.
- [Customer mix] Government customers are a material and volatile slice of revenue — the deck shows a private/government split of 79%/21% in FY2024, 73%/27% in FY2025 and 71%/29% in FY2026.
- [Market context] The India industrial gases market is put at $1.31 Bn by value in CY2024, expected to grow at ~7.5% CAGR from 2024 to 2028; by product Oxygen is 35.9%, Nitrogen 23.6%, Hydrogen 16.2%, Carbon Dioxide 11.2%, Argon & Mixtures 10.2%, Others 2.9% (F&S Report).
- [Pricing] "Argon prices remain on a recovery trajectory, showing a modest increase on a sequential basis, albeit still below H1 FY26 levels", while "Oxygen and Nitrogen prices remain stable" — margin gains are therefore only partly price-led.
- [Leadership] Chairman & Managing Director Padam Kumar Agarwala (40+ years, oversees the eastern region) and Joint Managing Director Varun Agarwal (15+ years, oversees the southern region, previously at Lehman Brothers); CFO K. Srinivas Prasad.
